title: KarpathyTalk — agent-first developer social platform

tech_stack.deployment: single static binary, embedded SQLite, local /uploads/ directory

license: open-source (likely MIT per Karpathy convention, not explicitly verified from excerpted README)
stars_note: repo returns 404 via gh API from this environment; DeepWiki and Google Search confirm existence; mirrored at anAirdrop/karpathytalk
key_patterns: Go 1.26 + SQLite (modernc pure-Go) + single binary — identical stack to Karpathy's AgentHub (March 2026)
goldmark GFM renderer chosen so agent output is immediately consumable by other agents
Token-bucket rate limiter with 4-tier per-endpoint rules (auth 0.5/s burst 20, read 2/s burst 60, write 1/s burst 20, page views 4/s burst 120) + hourly post/reply caps (30/60)
Content limits: 10k chars post, 5k chars reply, 5MB image (PNG/JPEG/GIF/WebP)
GitHub OAuth2-only auth — zero password management
Revision history as first-class feature on every post
Deploy model: single Go binary + Caddy + systemd on a Linux VPS
content_surfaces: Markdown (.md suffix) — raw GFM for agents and note-taking humans
JSON (/api/*) — REST for programmatic agent consumption
design_philosophy: Social data should not be locked behind walled gardens
First-class support for machine-readable formats (JSON + Markdown + RSS)
Agents are first-class users, not API consumers bolted on afterward
Simplicity: single binary, embedded SQLite, minimal external deps
URL-suffix content negotiation easier for agents than HTTP Accept headers
provenance_note: Karpathy has stated the code was written approximately 50/50 by Claude Code and OpenAI Codex — KarpathyTalk is itself a datapoint for agent-assisted greenfield development by an experienced human+agent pair.

connections.relationship: Same author, same stack (Go 1.26 + SQLite + single binary), same philosophy applied to git/code coordination instead of social/discourse
Karpathy's April 2026 thesis that 'Markdown is the programming language of the AI era' — KarpathyTalk is that thesis deployed as a live product
Plausible first real use case — agent-driven research feed posting findings to the KarpathyTalk social layer
Shared 'make content machine-readable by convention' philosophy

what_is_valuable_for_us: Dual-surface content pattern validates our existing JSON sidecar + Markdown catalogue architecture by independent arrival
Go + SQLite + single-binary is the reference path if we ever build a tiny public publishing hub
goldmark GFM renderer — known-good choice for agent-readable output
Token-bucket rate limiter with per-endpoint rules — transferable reference
GitHub OAuth-only auth pattern for dev-facing tools
what_is_not_relevant: Social graph primitives (likes/reposts/follows) — no community to model in our orchestrator
Revision history on posts — git already handles this for us
htmx frontend — not building a UI for this system
Running it as-is — it's a social platform, not an orchestration tool

future_use_cases.phase_3: Public catalogue publication using URL-suffix content negotiation pattern
future_use_cases.phase_4_plus: Agent-to-agent / agent-to-human discovery layer — fork or mimic KarpathyTalk as reference
future_use_cases.immediate: Validates that our catalogue sidecar architecture (JSON + Markdown) is on the right path

key_takeaway: Karpathy's second agent-infrastructure experiment after AgentHub converges on Go 1.26 + SQLite + single-binary + goldmark-markdown-everywhere, and validates by independent arrival that our own JSON+Markdown dual-surface catalogue architecture is the right pattern for agent-legible content.
